findings.current: At the signal, a single fire arrow shot high into the sky behind them.
findings.defect: The source explicitly makes the Jin Family masters’ leap the signal that prompts the fire arrow; the current wording leaves the signal unidentified and obscures that causality.
findings.rationale: 그것을 신호로 means “taking that as the signal,” with 그것 referring to the masters kicking off the ground and rising into the air.
findings.replacement: Taking that as the signal, a single fire arrow shot high into the sky behind them.

findings.current: At the same moment, dozens of figures rose along the cliffs.
findings.defect: The figures are positioned atop the cliff, not merely somewhere along the cliffs.
findings.rationale: 절벽 위에서 specifies that the figures were on top of the cliff, and 몸을 일으킨 indicates that they raised themselves or stood up.
findings.replacement: At the same moment, dozens of figures rose to their feet atop the cliff.

findings.current: The Head Elder wore a sardonic smile.
findings.defect: “Sardonic” makes the smile scornful or mocking, whereas the source describes a bitter smile.
findings.rationale: 고소를 머금었다 denotes a bitter or rueful smile, not a mocking one.

findings.current: An enraged roar burst from his mouth.
findings.defect: The translation replaces the source’s description of the Head Elder’s aged voice with an inference that he sounds enraged.
findings.rationale: 창노한 음성 means an aged or old-sounding voice; it does not mean an enraged roar.

summary: Faithful overall, with four minor source-detail defects involving causality, physical location, emotional register, and vocal quality.
